passage:
"Tanuja, get up. The bus comes in twenty minutes."
"Five more minutes, Amma."
"That's what you said ten minutes ago."
Tanuja pulled the sheet over her head. "I'm so tired."
Sangeeta sat on the bed. "The tablet light was on under your door at midnight."
"I just had one level left..."
"And yesterday you cried over your spelling test and shouted at Ravi."
Tanuja peeked out. "I didn't mean to. I just felt all scratchy."
"That's what no sleep does. So what if the tablet sleeps in the kitchen after nine?"
"Nine thirty?"
"Nine, on school nights. Nine thirty on Fridays."
Tanuja groaned, then nodded. "Fine. But you have to remind me."
"Deal."

qa.q: Where will the tablet sleep after nine?
qa.a: It will sleep in the kitchen after nine.

qa.q: How did Tanuja feel the day after gaming at midnight?
qa.a: She felt tired and scratchy, which is why she cried over her spelling test and shouted at Ravi.

qa.q: What went right in this conversation between Sangeeta and Tanuja?
qa.a: Sangeeta linked the tiredness to the late tablet use and they agreed together on a cut-off time and a place outside the bedroom.

qa.q: How might Ravi have felt when Tanuja shouted at him?
qa.a: Ravi was probably hurt or confused, not knowing Tanuja was short of sleep.

grounding: It shows a schoolchild struggling to wake and stay calm after late gaming, and a family agreeing a cut-off time and keeping the device out of the bedroom.

passage:
Last month I kept watching videos on Papa's old phone under my blanket. I told myself they were short, so they didn't count. But I would look up and it would be really late.
In the mornings my head felt full of cotton. In maths I read the same question three times. At lunch Kalyani asked to borrow my eraser and I snapped at her for no reason. She went quiet and sat with someone else.
After that, Mummy and I made a rule: the phone charges on the hall shelf after dinner, and I read a comic in bed instead. The first night was boring. Now I wake up before my alarm sometimes. I said sorry to Kalyani, too.

Vandana, Class 5

qa.q: Where does the phone charge after dinner now?
qa.a: The phone charges on the hall shelf after dinner.

qa.q: How did Vandana feel after snapping at Kalyani?
qa.a: Vandana probably felt bad and a little lonely when Kalyani went quiet and sat with someone else, which is why Vandana later said sorry.

qa.q: What small step helped Vandana most?
qa.a: Keeping the phone on the hall shelf and reading a comic in bed instead meant Vandana could sleep and wake up fresh.

qa.q: What was it like for Kalyani when Vandana snapped?
qa.a: It was probably hurtful and confusing for Kalyani, because she only asked for an eraser.

grounding: It shows a schoolchild whose late-night watching makes waking and focusing hard, and how keeping the device out of the bedroom protects sleep.

passage: Tomas, eleven, had a secret. After lights-out in the Prague flat, he played games under the blanket till one or two. In the mornings his mother had to shake him three times. At school his eyes felt full of sand. When his friend Xin bumped his desk in maths, Tomas snapped at him so loudly the teacher looked up. Later, embarrassed, he told his parents the truth. Instead of just taking the tablet away, they sat down together. 'What if all devices, ours too, charge in the kitchen from nine?' his father said. Tomas grumbled. The first two nights he lay awake, bored. By the fourth, he fell asleep reading. On Friday he said sorry to Xin, and he answered two questions in maths.

qa.q: Where did the devices charge from nine?
qa.a: In the kitchen.

qa.q: How did Tomas feel after snapping at Xin?
qa.a: He felt embarrassed, knowing he had been rude because he was so tired.

qa.q: Why did the family plan work better than just taking the tablet away?
qa.a: Everyone agreed to it, including the parents, so it felt fair and protected Tomas's sleep.

qa.q: How might Xin have felt when Tomas snapped at him?
qa.a: Xin was probably surprised and hurt, since he had only bumped the desk.

grounding: Shows a child who plays late into the night and struggles to wake, focus and stay calm, and an agreed device cut-off outside the bedroom protecting sleep.

passage: At the boarding school in Dehradun, Farhan, twelve, kept a phone hidden in his pillowcase and watched videos till two. By third period he was nodding off, and he'd started crying over small things, like a lost eraser. The housemaster, Wasim Sir, found the phone during a dorm check. He didn't shout. He sat on the end of the bed. 'You're falling asleep in class and you're upset all the time. Is it this?' Farhan nodded, ashamed. 'Let's make a deal. Phones go in the locker at nine-thirty, for everyone in this dorm, and you can use it at weekends.' Farhan grumbled. But after a week of real sleep, he was awake in class and laughing again at dinner.

qa.q: Where did Farhan hide the phone?
qa.a: In his pillowcase.

qa.q: How did Farhan feel when Wasim Sir found the phone?
qa.a: He felt ashamed but also recognised that the phone was why he was so tired and upset.

qa.q: What made Wasim Sir's response effective?
qa.a: He stayed calm, connected the phone to Farhan's tiredness, and made an agreed cut-off for the whole dorm.

qa.q: How might Farhan's classmates notice the change?
qa.a: They probably saw him awake in class and laughing at dinner instead of nodding off or crying.

grounding: Shows a child who watches videos late at night and struggles to wake, focus and stay calm, and an agreed cut-off with devices away from the bed protecting his sleep.

passage:
Sunday: Varun, ten, gamed on the laptop until midnight. His father Darshan was asleep and didn't notice.
Monday: Varun couldn't get up for school. At breakfast he burst into tears over burnt toast, and in class he forgot his homework.
Tuesday: Darshan sat with him after dinner. 'What's going on, champ?' Varun admitted the gaming. Together they made a rule: laptop off at eight-thirty and it stays on the dining table overnight.
Friday: Varun woke before his alarm. 'I feel less grumpy,' he told Darshan, surprised.

qa.q: What did Varun burst into tears over on Monday?
qa.a: Burnt toast.

qa.q: How did Varun feel on Monday morning?
qa.a: He felt exhausted and upset, crying easily and forgetting his homework.

qa.q: What rule did Varun and Darshan make together?
qa.a: The laptop goes off at eight-thirty and stays on the dining table overnight.

qa.q: How might Darshan feel when Varun says he feels less grumpy?
qa.a: He is probably relieved and pleased that the rule they made together is working.

grounding: Shows a child whose late-night gaming makes it hard to wake, focus and stay calm, and an agreed cut-off with the device outside the bedroom protecting sleep.

passage: Beta, you want the tablet in your room? Sit, and let your Hansa Dadi tell you about your papa, Deepak, when he was eleven. We gave him a video-game box for his birthday, and he kept it beside his bed. Every night I heard little beeps till past midnight. In the mornings he was a bear. He missed the school bus twice, dozed off in a maths test and shouted at me over a lost sock. Then his class teacher phoned: "Deepak seems so tired and cross lately." That night your Dadaji and Deepak sat down and agreed: games until eight, then the box lives in the drawing room. He sulked for three days. The next week he was up before me, whistling. So, where should your tablet sleep?

qa.q: Where did Deepak keep the video-game box at first?
qa.a: Beside his bed.

qa.q: What was young Deepak feeling on those mornings, and what shows it?
qa.a: He was tired and cross; he missed the bus, dozed off in a test and shouted over a lost sock.

qa.q: What turning point in the story changed Deepak's mornings?
qa.a: After the teacher's call, Dadaji and Deepak agreed on games until eight and the box living in the drawing room.

qa.q: How might Deepak's class teacher have seen him before the change?
qa.a: The teacher saw a boy who seemed tired and cross, and was concerned enough to phone home.

grounding: Illustrates a schoolchild gaming into the night who struggles to wake, focus and stay calm, and an agreed cut-off with the device outside the bedroom protecting sleep.
